claim: La Villa Madie is a Three Stars restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide France, located in Cassis at Anse de Corton
quote: La Villa Madie – Cassis – a MICHELIN Guide Restaurant. Three Stars: Exceptional cuisine, worth a special journey.

claim: La Villa Madie earned its third Michelin star in 2022; previously held two stars since 2014; run by Dimitri and Marielle Droisneau since 2013
quote: The restaurant earned its 'third star in 2022' and previously received a second star in 2014.

claim: La Villa Madie offers three tasting menus: €195 (4-course), €295 (6-course), €380 (8-course); menus change daily based on Mediterranean and garden produce
quote: prepared daily according to the mood of our Mediterranean, the growth of our gardens, and our orchards.

claim: La Villa Madie is open Thursday to Sunday (Mon–Wed closed year-round except June 15–Aug 31 2026); lunch 12:00–13:00, dinner 19:30–20:45; dress code chic and relaxed; credit card guarantee required
quote: The dress code is chic and relaxed. Men are required to wear long trousers and closed shoes.

claim: La Villa Madie features panoramic sea views overlooking the Bay of Cassis and Cap Canaille cliffs; sommelier Lionel Legoinha curates 550+ vintages including local Cassis wines; notable dishes include Royal Lobster with Saffron Broth and Rabbit with Palamos Prawns
quote: Panoramic sea views overlooking the Bay of Cassis and Cap Canaille cliffs. Modern design with large bay windows and expansive summer terrace.

claim: The 2026 MICHELIN Guide France & Monaco lists 668 starred establishments: 31 Three Stars, 84 Two Stars, 553 One Star
quote: 668 Michelin starred establishments: 31 Three Stars, 84 Two Stars and 553 One Star.

claim: La Villa Madie is the only 3-star Michelin restaurant listed for Cassis; there are no 2-star restaurants in Cassis
quote: Cassis 3 Stars MICHELIN Restaurants – the MICHELIN Guide France

claim: Marseille's Michelin-starred restaurants are either 3-star or 1-star; no 2-star restaurants are listed for Marseille or the surrounding area
quote: Le Petit Nice Passedat, AM par Alexandre Mazzia, and La Villa Madie are the three-star establishments in the Marseille area.

claim: Le Petit Nice Passedat holds 3 Michelin stars and is located in Marseille on the Corniche; has held 3 stars since 2008
quote: Le Petit Nice – Marseille – a MICHELIN Guide Restaurant. Three Stars: Exceptional cuisine.

claim: Le Petit Nice serves exclusively fish and seafood with no meat; menus range from €230 (lunch) to €490; signature dish is the 'My Bouille Abaisse' served in three courses for €390
quote: the Mediterranean reigns supreme, because everything changes in line with the seasons, the weather and catch.

claim: AM par Alexandre Mazzia holds 3 Michelin stars in Marseille; only 24 covers; cuisine blends Congo childhood and Japanese influences
quote: Three Stars: Exceptional cuisine, worth a special journey.

claim: AM par Alexandre Mazzia serves a tasting menu of 20–30 tiny dishes for lunch from €115–€265 and dinner from €215–€345
quote: Culinary voyage inspired by Congo childhood memories; signature dishes include smoked eel chocolate and algae popcorn.

claim: AM par Alexandre Mazzia offers 30 tiny dishes in a lunch tasting; wine pairings available at €145
quote: A lunch tasting menu offers approximately thirty different items at 175 euros.

claim: La Table du Castellet at Hôtel du Castellet (Le Castellet, ~35km from Cassis) holds 3 Michelin stars; Christophe Bacquié departed in 2024 and new chef Fabien Ferré now leads
quote: Christophe Bacquié and his wife Alexandra have stepped down from their management roles at the Hotel du Castellet after thirteen years.

claim: Le Petit Nice Passedat has been at 3 stars since 2008; AM par Alexandre Mazzia received its 3rd star in 2021; both are in Marseille about 25km from Cassis
quote: The temple of fish & seafood in Marseille — Le Petit Nice with emphasis on local rockfish and refined sauces.
